narrative.text: October: Humid to wet conditions across southern and southwestern catchments Baro-Akobo, Wabi Shebelle, Genale Dawa, Ogaden, and Abay support initial surface water accumulation.
November: Moisture shifts southward; wet to very wet conditions continue in Genale Dawa, Wabi Shebelle, Baro- Akobo, Ogaden, and parts of Abay Rift Valley, while northern areas dry out.

December: Dry to arid conditions dominate northern, central, and eastern basins Afar-Denakil, Aysha, middle upper Abay, Tekeze, and Awash. Sub-humid to wet levels persist in Omo-Gibe, Rift Valley, Baro-Akobo, Genale Dawa, Wabi Shebelle, and middle lower Ogaden.
January: Arid conditions expand across most northern, central, and eastern catchments. Sub-humid to wet conditions remain confined to Omo-Gibe, Rift Valley, and upper Genale Dawa.

summary.title: ICPAC — All Ethiopia
summary.text: Category agreement of 94.5% within the compared area, which covers 45% of the analysed national area. Predominant category in both: above normal. Periods differ (Oct 2026–Dec 2026 vs Oct 2026–Jan 2027).

summary.title: ICPAC — ONDJ R3 (Deyr) rainfall domain
summary.text: Category agreement of 100% within the compared area, which covers >99% of the analysed domain. Predominant category in both: above normal. Periods differ (Oct 2026–Dec 2026 vs Oct 2026–Jan 2027).

summary.title: EMI — sampled neighbourhoods near the zone arrows
summary.text: Opposing categories near the arrow of zone III: platform below normal, EMI above normal. Both favour above normal near the arrows of zones VI, VII and VIII. Sampled neighbourhoods (±0.5°), not complete EMI zones.

summary.title: EMI — sampled neighbourhoods near the zone arrows in the domain
summary.text: Both favour above normal near the arrows of zones VI, VII and VIII. The samples near zones VI and VII only partly overlap the domain (44% and 69% of sample cells); the values describe the whole sample. Sampled neighbourhoods (±0.5°), not complete EMI zones.

summary.title: EMI — whole zones (rainfall regions)
summary.text: Platform area mean of local probabilities over each EMI zone, below / near / above: zone III (Southwest): opposing: platform below normal, EMI above normal, platform 47% / 25% / 28%; zone VI (South Highland): both favour above normal, platform 21% / 24% / 55%; zone VII (South): both favour above normal, platform 24% / 26% / 50%; zone VIII (South-Southeast lowlands): both favour above normal, platform 18% / 24% / 58%. Zone boundaries: EMI homogeneous rainfall regions as published in 2013 (Korecha and Sorteberg), assumed unchanged for 2026/27.

summary.title: EMI — whole zones (rainfall regions)
summary.text: Platform area mean of local probabilities over each EMI zone, below / near / above: zone VI (South Highland): both favour above normal, platform 21% / 24% / 55% over the whole zone (66% of it in the domain); zone VII (South): both favour above normal, platform 24% / 26% / 50% over the whole zone (71% of it in the domain); zone VIII (South-Southeast lowlands): both favour above normal, platform 18% / 24% / 58% over the whole zone (99% of it in the domain). Zone boundaries: EMI homogeneous rainfall regions as published in 2013 (Korecha and Sorteberg), assumed unchanged for 2026/27.

summary.title: Robustness of the extraction
summary.text: The EMI category relationships are stable under the tested location and neighbourhood changes (100 variants per zone: half-widths 0.25–1.0°, arrow-tip shifts up to ±0.5°). With the ICPAC map as digitized and shifted by one source pixel in each direction, the All Ethiopia category agreement stays between 94.5% and 95.0%. With the ICPAC map as digitized and shifted by one source pixel in each direction, the ONDJ R3 (Deyr) rainfall domain category agreement stays at 100%. These are bounded sensitivity checks of the extraction, not statistical confidence intervals; exact EMI zone comparisons remain unavailable.

paragraphs.text: The platform favours below-normal rainfall near the arrow of EMI zone III, while the EMI outlook favours above-normal rainfall. This indicates disagreement in the favoured rainfall category. EMI prints 20% / 25% / 55% (below / near / above); the platform's area mean of local probabilities in the sampled neighbourhood is 50% / 31% / 19%. Over the whole zone (the EMI Southwest rainfall region), the platform area mean is 47% / 25% / 28%: opposing categories.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions near the arrow of EMI zone VI. EMI prints 15% / 25% / 60% (below / near / above); the platform's area mean of local probabilities in the sampled neighbourhood is 22% / 24% / 54%. Over the whole zone (the EMI South Highland rainfall region), the platform area mean is 21% / 24% / 55%: same category.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions near the arrow of EMI zone VII. EMI prints 25% / 15% / 60% (below / near / above); the platform's area mean of local probabilities in the sampled neighbourhood is 24% / 21% / 55%. Over the whole zone (the EMI South rainfall region), the platform area mean is 24% / 26% / 50%: same category.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions near the arrow of EMI zone VIII. EMI prints 10% / 15% / 75% (below / near / above); the platform's area mean of local probabilities in the sampled neighbourhood is 19% / 24% / 57%. Over the whole zone (the EMI South-Southeast lowlands rainfall region), the platform area mean is 18% / 24% / 58%: same category.

For every EMI zone, the platform value is the area mean of local probabilities within ±0.5° of the arrow tip, not the complete EMI zone: the figure publishes no zone boundaries and no reference period, so exact zone probability differences are not calculated.

Above-normal rainfall is the predominant tendency in both outlooks over their shared displayed area in Ethiopia, with localized disagreement. ICPAC shows a favoured category on 46% of Ethiopia and no forecast category shown (the legend does not explain the grey areas) on 54%; where it shows one it favours above normal on >99%, most often at 70-80% and 80-90%. The platform favours above normal on 71% and below normal on 17% of Ethiopia. There is category agreement of 94.5% within the compared area, which covers 45% of the analysed national area; opposite categories (above vs below) on 5% of the compared area. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so probabilities are not differenced. The official outlook covers Oct 2026–Dec 2026 and the platform Oct 2026–Jan 2027 (Jan 2027 only in the platform), so this compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

Both outlooks favour above normal rainfall throughout the part of the ONDJ R3 (Deyr) rainfall domain where both show a favoured category. ICPAC shows a favoured category on >99% of the ONDJ R3 (Deyr) rainfall domain and no forecast category shown (the legend does not explain the grey areas) on <1%; where it shows one it favours above normal on 100%, most often at 70-80% and 80-90%. The platform favours above normal on 100% and below normal on 0% of the ONDJ R3 (Deyr) rainfall domain. There is category agreement of 100% within the compared area, which covers >99% of the analysed domain. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so probabilities are not differenced. The official outlook covers Oct 2026–Dec 2026 and the platform Oct 2026–Jan 2027 (Jan 2027 only in the platform), so this compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

Not calculated: rainfall-anomaly differences, because no official rainfall-amount anomaly product was found in the checked ICPAC and EMI products; which forecast is more accurate, because that needs observations and a separate verification design (see Verification); same-event probability differences, because the target windows or spatial supports differ and ICPAC publishes only favoured-category intervals.

Favoured category: the leading tercile where it reaches 40% (the map display rule); otherwise no clear category.
An OND probability cannot be built by averaging monthly probabilities; ONDJ and OND are compared only as spatial tendencies.
